title: Set 37

sentences.ko: 봄에 빵 굽는 데 완전 빠져서 한 달쯤 주말마다 한 덩이씩 구웠는데, 밀가루가 떨어지고 나서는 더 사는 걸 계속 미루다가 결국 안 샀어. 발효종은 아직도 냉장고 안쪽에 그대로 있어.
sentences.text: I got really into baking bread back in the spring, and I made a loaf every weekend for like a month, but then I ran out of flour and never got around to buying more. The starter's still sitting in the back of my fridge.

alts.text: Back in the spring I was super into baking bread, and I was making a loaf every weekend for like a month, then I ran out of flour and just never bought more. That starter's still sitting in the back of my fridge.

I became quite interested in baking bread back in the spring, and I made a loaf every weekend for about a month, but then I ran out of flour and never managed to buy more. The starter is still sitting at the back of my refrigerator.

sentences.note: **got really into** 는 어떤 일에 푹 빠졌다는 뜻입니다. **never got around to** 는 하려고는 했는데 계속 미루다 결국 못 했다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 샌드위치 두 개랑 커피 두 잔 시켰는데 30달러가 나왔어. 계산대 앞에서 나도 모르게 소리내서 한마디 했지 뭐야. 이제 나도 예전엔 이게 얼마였는데 하고 떠드는 사람이 된 거지.
sentences.text: We got two sandwiches and two coffees and it came out to thirty bucks, and I actually said something out loud right there at the counter, so now I'm that guy who talks about what stuff used to cost.

alts.text: Two sandwiches, two coffees, thirty bucks, and I actually said something out loud right there at the counter, so yeah, now I'm that guy who talks about what stuff used to cost.

We ordered two sandwiches and two coffees, and the total came to thirty dollars. I actually said something aloud right there at the counter, so I have now become the sort of person who remarks on what things used to cost.

sentences.note: **came out to** 는 합계가 얼마 나왔다는 뜻입니다. **that guy who** 는 그런 부류의 사람이 돼 버렸다고 스스로를 놀리는 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 난방이 밤새 켜졌다 꺼졌다 해서 여기 아무도 못 자고 있어요. 기사님 일정이 꽉 찼다고 하신 건 아는데, 이번 주 안에 누구든 좀 보내 주실 수 있을까요? 목요일에 영하로 떨어진다고 하거든요.
sentences.text: The heat's been clicking on and off all night, so nobody in here is sleeping, and I know you said your guy is booked, but can you get somebody out this week? Because it's supposed to drop below freezing Thursday.

alts.text: Nobody in here's sleeping, the heat keeps clicking on and off all night. I know your guy's booked, but can you get somebody out this week? It's supposed to drop below freezing Thursday.

The heating has been switching on and off all night, so no one here is able to sleep. I understand that your technician is fully booked, but could you send someone out this week? The temperature is expected to fall below freezing on Thursday.

sentences.note: **get somebody out** 은 사람을 그 집까지 보내 달라는 뜻입니다. **booked** 는 일정이 예약으로 꽉 찼다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 아랫집 음악이 바닥으로 다 올라와요. 크지도 않고 저음만 울리는 거라 이런 말 꺼내는 것도 우습긴 한데, 그 소리 덮으려고 한 달째 선풍기 틀어 놓고 자고 있어요.
sentences.text: I can hear their music through the floor, and it's not even loud, it's just the bass, so I feel ridiculous even bringing it up. But I've been sleeping with a fan on for a month now just to cover it.

alts.text: Their music comes right up through the floor, and it's not even loud, it's just the bass, so I feel kinda ridiculous even bringing it up. But I've had a fan on all night for a month now just to cover it.

I can hear their music through the floor. It is not even loud, it is only the bass, so I feel ridiculous even raising the matter. However, I have been sleeping with a fan running for a month now simply to mask it.

sentences.note: **bringing it up** 은 어떤 얘기를 꺼낸다는 뜻입니다. **cover** 는 여기서 다른 소리로 덮어서 안 들리게 한다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 지하철이 늦게 다닌다고 둘러댔는데, 그 사람이 자기도 지난주에 똑같은 일이 있었다는 거야. 그냥 알람 못 듣고 잤다고 할 걸 그랬어, 괜히 더 찜찜해.
sentences.text: I told her the trains were running slow, and then she said the same thing happened to her last week, so now I feel worse than if I'd just admitted I slept through my alarm.

alts.text: So I go, oh the trains are running slow. And she's like, yeah that happened to me last week too. Now I kinda wish I'd just said I slept through my alarm.
I told her that the trains were running slowly, and she then said the same thing had happened to her last week, so I now feel worse than if I had simply admitted that I slept through my alarm.

sentences.note: **slept through my alarm** 은 알람이 울렸는데 못 듣고 계속 잤다는 뜻입니다. **running slow** 는 열차가 평소보다 늦게 다닌다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 1번 casual 의 "I did a loaf every weekend" 는 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 말이라 "I was making a loaf every weekend" 로 고쳤습니다.
3번 casual 이 text 의 어순만 바꾼 수준이라, 더 짧고 축약된 구어(here's, guy's, keeps clicking)로 다시 썼습니다.
5번 casual 이 text 와 거의 같은 문장이었습니다(앞머리 두 마디만 달랐음). 말할 때 나오는 인용법(I go / she's like)으로 완전히 다시 썼습니다.
5번 한국어의 마지막 "지금이 더 찜찜해" 가 툭 끊겨 어색해서 앞 문장에 이어 붙였습니다.
